To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

airborne cocaine concentrations in urban areas are in line with consumption prevalence, and that airborne cocaine concentrations do not seem to be associated with adverse health outcomes in the general population, at least in the investigated Italian cities.
airborne drugs are not a health risk, but can be used to estimate the drug abuse prevalence in urban areas.
the airborne cocaine concentration is related to consumption and can be used to assess the abuse prevalence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(i) the assessment of drug abuse in a city, (ii) the evaluation of the sanitary effects of airborne drugs, and (iii) the development of a monitoring system of drug-related health risks.
the social and health relevance of airborne illicit drug concentrations.
the development of a methodology to assess illicit drug abuse in urban areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the airborne drug concentrations, in spite of being very low, can be used to estimate consumption, but the health effects, if any, need further studies.

the drug abuse assessment based on airborne drug measurements can be considered as an interesting and useful complementary approach, but not as an alternative to the more consolidated waste water approach.

airborne monitoring is a feasible tool for assessing drug abuse, but the results should be carefully interpreted and the data should be compared with those of other approaches, in particular the waste waters monitoring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the airborne cocaine concentrations can be used to assess drug abuse prevalence, but the concentrations are too low to cause any health effect.
the airborne cocaine monitoring can be used to assess drug abuse in the cities, but it cannot be considered an indicator of the sanitary impact of the drugs.
, in the future, airborne drug monitoring could be used to assess the drug burden in a given area and, possibly, to estimate the prevalence of drug abuse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
airborne drugs can be used for monitoring drug abuse and, in the case of illicit drugs, for drug control.

, in order to assess drug abuse, the environmental approach must consider all the factors that determine the airborne burden of drugs, and that, in order for the environmental approach to be effective, it should be integrated with other monitoring approaches.
airborne drugs are a potential tool to assess drug abuse prevalence and to identify the areas and the times when the consumption is higher, but they cannot be considered a proxy of drug abuse.
